channel.title: Infiniti recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Nissan Armada and Infiniti QX80 Incorrect Weight Label
item.description: On certain Nissan Armada and Infiniti QX56/QX80 vehicles equipped with 22-inch wheels, the axle weight rating shown on the vehicle's certification label is incorrect. Because the number is wrong, an owner could load the vehicle beyond what it can safely carry. Nissan will correct the problem by installing new certification labels on the vehicle and mailing replacement labels directly to owners.

item.title: Nissan and Infiniti rearview camera may not show image
item.description: Nissan is recalling certain 2025 Murano, 2025-2026 Armada, and Infiniti QX80 vehicles. A software error in the infotainment system, the main screen in the dashboard, can occur when the vehicle starts up, and then the rearview camera picture does not appear when the driver shifts into reverse. Because of that, these vehicles do not meet the federal rear visibility safety rule. A dealer can update the software, or the update can be sent to the vehicle over the air.

item.title: Nissan, Infiniti Engine Bearings May Fail
item.description: Certain engines in these vehicles use bearings that may have a manufacturing defect. Over time, this defect can lead to the engine failing. In some cases, a failed bearing can cause a break in the engine block, which allows hot oil inside the engine to leak out while the vehicle is being driven.

item.title: Nissan Murano, Pathfinder, QX60 Brake Caliper May Break
item.description: Nissan is recalling certain Murano, Pathfinder, and INFINITI QX60 vehicles because one or both front brake caliper assemblies may have reduced strength and could break while the vehicle is being driven. If a caliper breaks, the vehicle can lose front brake function on that side, making it harder to slow down and stop the vehicle.

item.title: Nissan Rogue and INFINITI QX80 Rearview Camera May Go Blank
item.description: A software error can leave the rearview camera screen blank when the vehicle is shifted into reverse. Instead of showing the view behind the vehicle, the display shows nothing. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet the federal rear visibility standard that requires that image to appear. The fix is a software update for the screen system, which can either be sent to the vehicle over the air or installed by a dealer.

item.title: Infiniti QX80 Backup Camera May Freeze or Go Blank
item.description: Some 2025 INFINITI QX80 SUVs have a software error in the Around View Monitor system. When the vehicle is shifted into reverse, the rearview camera image can freeze and go blank instead of showing what is behind the vehicle. This means the driver may lose the rearview camera image while backing up, so they cannot rely on it to see what is behind the vehicle.

item.title: Infiniti Q50 and Q70 driveshaft can break
item.description: Nissan is recalling certain Infiniti Q50, Q70, and Q70L two-wheel drive vehicles because the driveshaft can develop fatigue and break.

item.title: Nissan Pathfinder, Infiniti QX60 seat belt pretensioner issue
item.description: On some 2024 Nissan Pathfinder and Infiniti QX60 vehicles, a part in the left front seat belt that tightens the belt in a crash may not be attached correctly. A rivet holding it in place is missing. Because of this, the seat belt may not hold the occupant properly if the vehicle crashes. Dealers will inspect the seat belt and replace it if needed.

item.title: Nissan and Infiniti driver airbags may deploy improperly
item.description: Nissan is recalling certain Nissan and Infiniti cars and SUVs because of a problem that happened during manufacturing. The inflator in the driver's airbag, which is the part that fills the bag, may absorb moisture. If that happens, the airbag may deploy improperly. Dealers will replace the entire driver's airbag assembly at no cost to the owner. Nissan mailed owner notification letters on April 10, 2024.

item.title: INFINITI QX60 Headlights May Aim Too Low at Speed
item.description: These Infiniti QX60 vehicles have headlights that adjust automatically as you drive. At certain high speeds, the system may aim the headlights downward when it should not. Headlights pointed the wrong way do not light the road as they are meant to, which cuts down on how well the driver can see. A dealer will change the settings in the module that controls the lights to correct the problem.

item.title: Nissan Rogue, Pathfinder, Infiniti QX60 Seat Weld Failure
item.description: In some Nissan Rogue and Pathfinder, and Infiniti QX60 vehicles, the driver's power seat may not be fully attached to its frame. Over time, the welds holding the seat frame to a bracket at the back of the seat can come apart. If this happens, the seat is not as sturdy as it should be. In a crash, a seat that isn't properly secured may not hold the driver in place the way it's supposed to.

item.title: Infiniti QX50, QX55 Front Door Lock May Not Latch
item.description: Nissan says some INFINITI QX50 and QX55 vehicles may have the wrong door latch installed in the front right passenger door. Because of this, the front right door lock may not lock automatically as it should. If the door is not locked, it could unlatch and open if the vehicle is involved in a crash.

item.title: Infiniti QX60 Second-Row Seat May Not Lock
item.description: On some 2023 Infiniti QX60 vehicles, the second-row adjustable seat may slide back farther than it should. It may also become hard to move, get stuck, or fail to lock into the correct position.

item.title: INFINITI QX60, Nissan Pathfinder Seat Track Bolt Missing
item.description: Some INFINITI QX60 and Nissan Pathfinder vehicles may have a second-row seat track that is missing a mounting bolt. This bolt is one of the parts required to anchor the seat belt system to the vehicle. Because the bolt may be missing, these vehicles do not meet a federal safety standard covering seat belt anchorages. The second-row seat track itself may not be as securely fastened to the vehicle as it should be as a result of this missing bolt.

item.title: Infiniti Q50, Q60 and QX80 rearview image may not display
item.description: Nissan is recalling certain Infiniti Q50, Q60, and QX80 vehicles because of a software error. The error can shut off the screen that handles audio and video, so the image from the rear-view camera does not appear. Because of this, these vehicles do not meet the federal rules for rear visibility. A dealer will update the software at no cost to the owner. Nissan mailed notification letters to owners, and the company has a customer service line for questions.

item.title: Nissan Murano and Infiniti Steering Parts May Crack
item.description: Some Nissan Murano and Infiniti Q50, QX50, and QX60 vehicles have a front steering knuckle or rear axle housing that may not be strong enough because of a manufacturing heat-treatment problem. If the part is struck hard, such as when a vehicle hits a curb, it could deform. That could cause the driver to lose steering control, or a wheel could separate from the vehicle.

item.title: Nissan Armada and INFINITI QX80 fuel pump may fail
item.description: Nissan is recalling certain Nissan Armada and INFINITI QX80 vehicles built with V8 engines. A part inside the fuel pump, the impeller, can swell and jam inside the pump housing. When that happens the fuel pump stops working, so the engine can no longer be supplied with fuel and can shut off while the vehicle is being driven.

item.title: Infiniti Q50, Q60 Engine May Stall From Fuel Loss
item.description: Infiniti is recalling certain Q50 and Q60 vehicles. These vehicles have a computer that manages engine performance. After the computer detects rapid acceleration, it may incorrectly reduce engine power and cut back the amount of fuel reaching the engine. This drop in fuel supply can leave the engine running low on fuel. When the engine does not get enough fuel, it may stall while the vehicle is being driven.

item.title: Infiniti QX50 Tire Information Placard May Be Illegible
item.description: Nissan (Infiniti) is recalling certain 2020 Infiniti QX50 vehicles because the text on the Tire and Loading Information placard, including the tire size and loading capacity, may be illegible. If an owner cannot read this information, the wrong size tire could be installed, or the vehicle could be overloaded, which increases the risk of a crash.

item.title: Infiniti Q60 Rear Seat Belts May Not Lock
item.description: Some Infiniti Q60 vehicles have rear seat belts built with a locking feature meant to help keep the belt snug during a crash that involves more than one impact. In some vehicles, this locking feature may not engage the way it is supposed to, so the seat belt may not tighten and hold the passenger as intended.

item.title: Nissan and Infiniti vehicles: brake fluid leak may cause fire
item.description: Nissan is recalling certain Nissan Murano, Maxima and Pathfinder and Infiniti QX60 vehicles. The part that controls the anti-lock brakes can let brake fluid leak onto a circuit board inside it. These vehicles were covered by an earlier recall and were either not repaired or were inspected and judged not to need a repair. This recall also covers more vehicles than the earlier one. Dealers will replace the anti-lock brake part at no cost to owners.

item.title: Nissan and Infiniti backup camera image can stay off
item.description: Nissan is recalling certain Nissan and Infiniti vehicles, including the Altima, Rogue, Sentra, Murano, Pathfinder, Titan, Frontier, Leaf, Versa and several Infiniti Q and QX models. The back-up camera and display settings can be changed so that the rear view picture no longer appears, and the vehicle keeps that setting the next time it is put in reverse. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet the federal rear visibility safety standard. Dealers will update the camera settings software at no cost.

item.title: INFINITI QX50 knee airbag cover may detach in crash
item.description: Nissan is recalling certain 2019 INFINITI QX50 vehicles. The passenger-side knee airbag has a trim cover that is meant to split along a built-in tear seam when the airbag goes off. In a crash that happens in very cold temperatures, that cover may instead separate from the knee airbag unit unexpectedly. INFINITI will notify owners, and retailers will replace the passenger-side knee airbag unit free of charge. The recall began October 23, 2018.

item.title: Infiniti QX30 Seat Belt Anchorage May Detach
item.description: On certain 2018 Infiniti QX30 vehicles, the bolt that holds the right-hand lower seat belt anchorage in place may not have been installed correctly during production. Because of this, the seat belt anchorage could detach if the vehicle is in a crash. As a result, these vehicles do not meet federal safety standards for seat belts and seat belt anchorages.

item.title: Infiniti QX30 Driver Air Bag May Deploy Unexpectedly
item.description: The steering components in your QX30 may not be grounded well enough. If static electricity builds up and discharges while the air bag's clockspring is broken, the driver's air bag can deploy on its own.

item.title: Infiniti Q50 Software Flaw Can Stall Engine
item.description: These vehicles have a computer that controls the fuel pump, and it may have incorrect software installed. Because of this software error, the system may not correctly track how much fuel remains in the main tank, and it can let the fuel level get too low to keep supplying fuel to the engine. When that happens, the engine can stall while you are driving.
